# VRFDefaultEditor

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Core.Editors.UI` · assembly `VRFramework.Core.Editors` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Editor/UI/VRFDefaultEditor.cs#L16)

The styled inspector a VRF script gets when it has no hand-written editor of its own. It
reads the serialized fields and lays them out in the framework's usual shape: ordinary
settings in one section, UnityEvents in the tinted section below.

This exists so the united look does not depend on somebody writing an editor for every
script. Deriving a one-line subclass with a `[CustomEditor]`attribute is enough;
see VRFDefaultEditors.cs. Multi-object editing comes along for free, because everything
is drawn straight from [`SerializedProperty`](https://docs.unity3d.com/ScriptReference/SerializedProperty.html).

```csharp
public class VRFDefaultEditor : VRFComponentEditor
```
